description: GDPR + CPRA compliance layer — consent capture, data subject rights (export/erase), cookie banner, and Record of Processing Activities. Composes onto fullstack-ts / nextjs-ts / ecommerce-headless.

buildHints.whenToUse: Shipping to EU / CA / other jurisdictions with data-subject rights obligations. Bolt onto an existing fullstack/api backend.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm validate` — confirms required files and key exports are present.
Run `pnpm build` — `tsc --noEmit` typechecks the full pack; zero errors expected.
Extend `EXAMPLE_ROPA` in `src/data-inventory.ts` with your actual data categories, legal bases, and retention periods.
Wire `/api/export-my-data` using `collectExport` from `src/data-subject-rights.ts` — must respond within 30 days per Art. 12(3).
Wire `/api/delete-my-data` using `honorErasure` — must honor erasure within 30 days unless an Art. 17(3) exception applies.
Drop `<CookieBanner>` at the root layout — consent MUST be gathered BEFORE setting any non-essential cookies.
Fill out `docs/DPIA-template.md` if you process high-risk categories (Art. 35).
gotchas: 'Consent' as a legal basis has SIX requirements per Art. 4(11) — freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, affirmative, withdrawable. Pre-ticked boxes are invalid.
Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) is often a better basis than consent for operational processing — but requires a documented LIA (Legitimate Interest Assessment).
Right-to-delete is NOT absolute. Exceptions: legal obligation, public interest, establishment of legal claims (Art. 17(3)). Document which exception applies when refusing.
Data breaches must be reported to the supervisory authority within 72 HOURS per Art. 33.
CPRA (California) has parallel but not identical rules — this pack covers the shared 80%; add CPRA-specific flows as needed.
architectureNotes: Replace `InMemoryConsentStore` with a DB-backed implementation before production — the in-memory store does not survive restarts.
`collectExport` fans out to per-category collectors; each collector returns its slice of the user's data. Add one collector per table/service that holds PII.
`honorErasure` runs `retentionChecks` before any erasers — pass all Art. 17(3) exception checkers there so refusals are documented before data is touched.
